description: This program elective gives an overview of some of the special machines used for control and industrial applications.

syllabus.title: Special Electrical Machines
syllabus.body: Construction, working, characteristics and applications of the following electrical machines: stepper motor, brushless DC motor, servomotors, shaded pole motor, reluctance motor, hysteresis motor, single phase series motor, repulsion motor, Schrage motor and linear induction motor.

syllabus.title: Slip Power Recovery Drives
syllabus.body: Concept of slip power in induction motors, static Kramer and Scherbius drives, static rheostatic control of induction motors. Rotor energy loss of cage induction motors during acceleration, stopping and reversal of speed, and time taken during acceleration.

syllabus.title: Brushless PMSM for Electric Vehicles
syllabus.body: Dynamic analysis of brushless PMSM control and its applications for electric vehicles.

syllabus.title: Wind Energy Based Asynchronous Generators
syllabus.body: Comparison with conventional generators, self-excited induction generator and wound rotor induction machine.

outcomes: Describe various industrial motors and drive systems.
Apply knowledge of power electronics to drive systems.
Learn speed control of EV drives in an energy efficient manner using power electronics.
textbooks: M. G. Say, Theory, Performance and Design of AC Machines, CBS Publishers.
A. S. Langsdorf, Theory of Alternating Current Machinery, CBS Publishers.
Ashfaq Hussain, Electric Machines, Dhanpat Rai and Co.
referenceBooks: I. J. Nagrath and D. P. Kothari, Electric Machines, Tata McGraw Hill.
B. K. Bose, Modern Power Electronics and AC Drives, PHI.
G. K. Dubey, Fundamentals of Electrical Drives, Narosa Publication.
